metadata.note: Major Pennsylvania Railroad passenger routes beyond the two already mapped (Philadelphia-Pittsburgh main and the New York-Washington corridor, both in pennsylvania_railroad.geojson). Covers the Fort Wayne Route to Chicago (the western half of the Broadway Limited's run), the Panhandle Route to St. Louis, the Northern Central to Elmira, the Philadelphia & Erie, the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines to Atlantic City, and the Cleveland & Pittsburgh. Geometry is hand-placed waypoints on the real cities and junctions each line served - NOT OpenStreetMap-traced track and not surveyed centerline - so curvature is approximate though the towns and topology are right. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from real timetables. REFINEMENT (2026-08-19): the Fort Wayne Route and Cleveland & Pittsburgh were densified from coarse waypoint chains to the full sequence of real division points and station towns each line served (Fort Wayne now via Sewickley, Rochester, Beaver Falls, Columbiana, Salem, Alliance, Canton, Massillon, Orrville, Wooster, Mansfield, Crestline, Bucyrus, Upper Sandusky, Ada, Lima, Delphos, Van Wert, Fort Wayne, Columbia City, Warsaw, Plymouth, Valparaiso, Gary and Whiting; Cleveland & Pittsburgh via Rochester, Midland, East Liverpool, Wellsville, Salineville, Bayard, Minerva, Alliance, Ravenna, Hudson and Bedford). These are still hand-placed town waypoints - an OpenStreetMap track trace was attempted but every Overpass API instance was unavailable at the time. GEOMETRY REFINED (2026-08-22): replaced the ~30-point approximation with a 57-point real-station waypoint list covering all four historic divisions (Pittsburgh-Steubenville via the West Virginia Panhandle towns of Crafton, Carnegie, Bridgeville, McDonald, Burgettstown, and Weirton/Hollidays Cove; Steubenville-Columbus via Mingo Junction, Toronto, Empire, Bergholz, Jewett, Cadiz Junction, Cadiz, New Rumley, Uhrichsville, Dennison, Gnadenhutten, Newcomerstown, Port Washington, Trinway, Newark, and Hebron; Columbus-Indianapolis via Harrisburg, Lilly Chapel, London, South Vienna, Springfield, Donnelsville, Urbana, St. Paris, Palestine, Richmond IN, Cambridge City, Knightstown, New Castle, Shirley, Anderson, and Pendleton; Indianapolis-St. Louis via Plainfield, Clayton, Greencastle, Cloverdale, Putnamville, Brazil, Terre Haute, Marshall IL, Casey, Mattoon, Effingham, Vandalia, Greenville, and Highland), per a detailed station list supplied directly by the user. Still straight-line segments between those stations, not surveyed track centerline. GEOMETRY UPGRADE (2026-08-23): the Panhandle Route (57-point hand-placed straight-line-between-stations version) was replaced with a 543-point real OpenStreetMap track trace (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search) -- Overpass is reachable again. This fixes visible backtracking/loop artifacts in the old version (e.g. near Steubenville, Cadiz, and around Dennison/Newark, OH) that came from straight-line jumps between individually-plotted town coordinates rather than following actual track. Traced length 1036.0 km / 643.8 mi, Pittsburgh to St. Louis. The other lines in this file (Fort Wayne Route, Cleveland & Pittsburgh, Northern Central, Philadelphia & Erie, Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines) remain hand-placed waypoint chains and were not touched in this pass. GEOMETRY UPGRADE ROUND 2 (2026-08-23): real-traced the four remaining hand-placed lines via OpenStreetMap/Overpass (shortest-path graph search), same fix already applied to the Panhandle Route. Fort Wayne Route: 64 -> 374 points, verified passing within 1km of Alliance and Canton, OH. Cleveland & Pittsburgh: 25 -> 3616 points, passes within 1km of Alliance, OH. Northern Central: 16 -> 566 points, passes within 1km of York, PA; one ~15km hand-bridged gap remains north of the PA/NY line where Overpass found no connected path even including abandoned track. Philadelphia & Erie: 14 -> 511 points. All four checked for backtracking (no loops/reversals found). The Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines (Camden-Atlantic City) was NOT converted -- Overpass found no connected path across the Pine Barrens for this corridor even with abandoned track included and a widened search box, so it remains a hand-placed waypoint chain (unchanged from before; it was not exhibiting loop artifacts to begin with). || Sodus Bay / Elmira Branch added 2026-08-24. Traced from OpenStreetMap: 147.0 km (91.4 miles) Sodus Point to Elmira, of which 139 km runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR or on the rail trails that occupy the ex-PRR right of way today (Sodus Point to Wallington Trail, Ontario Pathways Rail Trail, Catharine Valley Trail). The last 6.4 km from Horseheads into Elmira is traced over today's Southern Tier Line because the PRR's own approach there is not separately tagged in OSM; Northern Central trains reached Elmira over the Northern Central main line (prr-northern-central). Largest straight-line link bridging a gap between fragments is 0.64 km. The line carried no passengers between November 15 1935 and its abandonment, so under CLAUDE.md Rule 1 it is not drawn for those years and there is no Penn Central-era feature for it, even though Penn Central did inherit the branch in 1968 and abandoned Seneca Castle to Newark in 1973. The Stanley-Canandaigua branch is not traced here.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Pittsburgh Fort Wayne and Chicago Railway, Main Line Pittsburgh to St. Louis, Northern Central Railway, Philadelphia and Erie Railroad, Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines, Cleveland and Pittsburgh Railroad), american-rails.com, trains.com, jbritton.pennsyrr.com
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-08-24), assembled by shortest path constrained to a 4 km corridor around the Wikimedia Commons Data:Elmira and Lake Ontario Railroad.map and Data:Canandaigua and Elmira Railroad.map geometry (CC BY 4.0).
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.company: Elmira and Lake Ontario Railroad / Northern Central Railway (Pennsylvania Railroad)
properties.speed_source: estimated: rural branch, steam then gas-electric; unsourced

segments.note: The Sodus Point & Southern (incorporated March 19 1852) opened between Sodus Point and Gorham on January 16 1873, meeting the Elmira, Jefferson & Canandaigua -- which the Northern Central had leased on January 19 1866 -- near Stanley, creating a through route from Lake Ontario to Elmira. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the references below cover this line, but nothing has been checked specifically against this segment's start year, end year or service. Treat the dates and the headway as unverified. Supporting references for the line:
Wikipedia (Pittsburgh Fort Wayne and Chicago Railway, Main Line Pittsburgh to St. Louis, Northern Central Railway, Phila…

segments.note: The Northern Central bought the Sodus line in 1884 and immediately built a coal trestle at Sodus Point; all the predecessors consolidated into the Elmira and Lake Ontario Railroad on December 31 1886. After the pier was enlarged in 1894 the branch carried four passenger trains a day each way between Elmira and Sodus Point -- the basis for this 360-minute headway.

segments.note: The lease passed to the Pennsylvania Railroad on January 1 1911 and the route became the PRR's Elmira Branch. Coal to the Sodus Point pier was the traffic that mattered; passenger revenue declined steadily through the 1920s.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the references below cover this line, but nothing has been checked specifically against this segment's start year, end year or service. Treat the dates and the headway as unverified. Supporting references for the line:

segments.note: Passenger trains ran until 1934 -- steam first, then a gas-electric car -- and a mixed train carried the last passengers until November 15 1935. The line itself carried coal for another three decades: the Elmira & Lake Ontario merged into the Northern Central January 31 1956, and the last boat loaded at the Sodus Point trestle on December 11 1967.
